Key pain: when using streaming mode with function schema the client-side JSON parser frequently fails (JSONDecodeError) because the streamed chunks sometimes include partial tokens and the model emits additional unexpected keys (e.g. "meta" or "debug_hint") that break strict schema validation. Customer quote: "It works in non-streaming tests but breaks in production streams — parser dies mid-stream."

Customer tech stack: Node.js backend (express) calling Redwood JS SDK v0.8. Using a small worker pool, low concurrency (20 qps), cost-sensitive. Latency target = ~200-500ms tail for agent responses.

They tried quick mitigations: set lower temperature, added post-stream buffer + rejoin logic, switched to non-streaming function calls (works but increases latency and cost). Reported observation: issues spike when responses include tool call results (web search plugin) — function schema validators complain about type mismatches (string vs object) and missing required fields.
